artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Psiaki complained that Covenant Presbyterian Church's Session erred in installing officers elected at a congregational meeting that excluded communicant members under age 18 from voting, in violation of the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint (15-5), holding that all communicant members have a constitutional right to vote in officer elections regardless of age, and that church bylaws may not override BCO provisions; multiple dissenting opinions argued that BCO 20-3 and 24-3's phrase 'good and regular standing' permits local sessions to establish reasonable minimum voting ages.

artifacts.synopsis: Dennis Lebo complained that Susquehanna Valley Presbytery erred in denying his complaint that the congregation of Carlisle Reformed Presbyterian Church acted unconstitutionally when it voted to supplement the Assistant Pastor's Fund. The SJC denied the complaint, finding that the congregation's action did not violate BCO 12-5b because the Session retained authority to approve and adopt the final budget.

4. The Northside Presbyterian Church Session acted out of accord with BCO 25-7 in proposing a revision of church bylaws.

4. The Session did not violate BCO 25-7 by indicating in its plan that the church's bylaws would be revised. A local church may, and often does, have bylaws. Such bylaws are envisioned, not prohibited, by BCO (see
BCO 25-7). There is no indication in the record that the Session intended to alter the PCA's BCO, or that the church's own bylaws would be out of accord with the BCO.

artifacts.synopsis: Parks and others challenged Northside Session's plan for multiple elder resignations, pastor severance, a delayed pastoral call, and bylaw revisions. The SJC denied every specification, holding that the plan did not violate BCO 24-6, 20-6, 20-2, or 25-7; a dissent was recorded.
